utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the preliminaries were postponed until later. Therefore, there are no preliminaries anymore. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Not a preliminary, just an indication that in response to Your Honours' request yesterday for original materials in respect of the document that was marked at P7618, thanks to the support and co-operation of colleagues in different sections of the building, we have, in court with us, the originals of those materials for Your Honours' inspection, and I just wanted you to be notified of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'd like to have a look at it. Has the Defence had an opportunity to look at it?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Not yet, Your Honour. And I just wanted to put this out and we're in Your Honours' hands as to how to procedurally you want to have a look at these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, we first allow the Defence to have a look at it and then the Chamber will look at it. Unless there's any objection by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If Mr. Lukic heard you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then, sooner or later, he'll find it on his desk and he'll ask himself what to do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would -- my colleague has another -- has a part of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- we discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher could already fetch the other part. Because I think what we saw yesterday started with the number 2, where I usually start counting at number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And if I may, Your Honours, because we've -- this document comes to you today in parts, I'd like to just briefly read out where those parts come from so that we're fully transparent about how the document has been used, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like do that or would you like to do that when you further introduce them, the parts?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd actually like to do it now, before Your Honours and my friend have a more detailed look at the documents. So 65 ter number -- what was 65 ter number 33148 and is now P7618 has an ERN range, the range of the entire document is 00269212 to 00269226.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's sequential.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes. So the originals of portions of that document have been admitted as exhibits in prior cases, and the range 00269215 to 00269218 was admitted as Exhibit P1840 in the Galic case; while 00269223 to 00269226 has been admitted as P586 in the Slobodan Milosevic case. Now, the Galic exhibit I just mentioned consists of pages 4 to 7 of P7618; while the Milosevic exhibit I mentioned consists of the cover sleeve and three photographs, pages 12 to 15, of P7618. Now, it may not necessarily make anything clearer, but what I'd felt I needed to do is put on the record the history of the handling of that ERN range so that Your Honours can understand why it comes to you today in parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I see that the ERN range starting with 00269212 starts with a page with a number 2 on it. I wonder, of course, where the number 1 preceding that would be.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We'll do what we can immediately to find it for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that the parties will have a look at it, because it still seems even as it is split up in two portions that it's still, here and there, mixed up one file with another one. That's -- and I invite the parties to also carefully compare the description of the incident with the photographs, the photographs which appear under a different number. And from what I think I saw yesterday, that the photographs may not be about the same incident as the remainder of the file is, and I especially draw your attention to the fact that in the description, I think the tiles on the ground are described as being 40 centimetres by 60 centimetres, which is a different shape from a -- it's rectangular rather than a -- than a square. And also there's a description about what is against the buildings to protect the ground floor. In the description, I think, it's 5 metres concrete high, whereas, on the pictures we see certainly some protection of a building but that also is, if you compare that with the persons walking by, certainly would not be 5 metres high and most likely is not of concrete. So I'm wondering still whether it's not two still mixed up, portions, the one dealing with one file and the other one dealing with two files, as a matter of fact. I leave it to the parties to see whether they can reach agreement whether -- and I think that's the main question, whether these photographs as we find them in these -- in this photo documentation, whether that is photo documentation which relates to what is elsewhere described in this investigative file. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. One more thing. We have cover page then that there was photo documentation in the case 431/93. Where is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that is also a very valid question. Let me just see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you just repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The number is 431/93.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's corrected now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Um, the file that was 65 ter number 33379 and 1D00742 contains -- and is now P7617 contains the photos related to not only 431/93, the contemporaneous investigation, but also the reconstruction of the crime scene that took place in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's not in what we see -- look at now.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No. This is -- what you see now is related to P7618, the subsequent document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- but I think the question we have a page in the -- if I could say so, in the 431 case, which says "5 foto dokumentacija" and then 431/93 and the date and mentioning the Trg Zavnobih, which means that the -- at least suggests that there has been a photo documentation of what is described in that file, and I think that's what Mr. Lukic is seeking, whether that is available as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's our position that those photos are what are contained in P7617.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That one is done in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your microphone was not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, I think you referred to the fact that that is a document which was created in 1995. Now, in itself --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, we have page 16 at least in B/C/S version. It says: Date of taking pictures, 16th of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the document my learned friend just quoted. So it's not from 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But an investigative file can be created at a later point in time, not before the incident. We'll have to carefully look at it and I hope you have some confidence, Mr. Lukic, that we're really carefully looking to sort this out --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do have confidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the file gives any suggestion that there must be already a photo documentation from 1993, or whether the file, rather, has -- gives clues to the photo documentation being produced only in 1995. We'll have to carefully look at that. I'll now return the two -- I keep them nicely apart. And I think it's now time for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One should be returned to the Prosecution and the other one stays in the hands of Madam Registrar because it's in her custody as admitted exhibits in another case. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just to be helpful, Your Honour, if everyone goes to P7617, page 8, you see there the photos from 1993. I just wanted to point that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In fact, page 8 is the cover page, and the photos begin at page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Obviously only in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page in B/C/S. Next page in B/C/S perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Next page in English so we can see what's the description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then we have to go to the next page in B/C/S as well. Because, in English, it's now photo 3. How many more photos are in this file?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's the last one, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If there's another one, then move to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On page 16, another series of photos appear, and I think this second series bears a date in 1995; whereas, the first series, Mr. Lukic, at least on the cover page, bears the year 1993 and it looks as if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to page 16. The next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Here we see the new year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the corresponding page in English, please. Obviously a reconstruction of the scene made in 1995 with respect to the event on 9th November 1993. Can we go to the next photograph, if there's another one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we now have a first impression of what is there. I think it raises quite a few other questions as well comparing description with photographs, but for the time being, let's move on, and let's have the witness enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To continue with this topic, is it possible if we -- if Ms. Stewart could play for us 1D05911, which is V000-0325-1-A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what are we supposed to look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This incident, I would start from the -- from the page 8, where it's cover page, saying that it's from 1993, and then I would go to page 9, where we can see those concrete barricades and on that movie we would try to show the real place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's my impression now that we're sort of bouncing from point to point by the counsel, which presumably implicates the reason why the Court wanted us to get together so we could come to an understanding of what we agreed on, perhaps what was in dispute and bring it back to the Court rather than going through that process in real time and in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I need the witness for this. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What -- I understand that you would like to play a video, Mr. Lukic, and you seek the assistance of the OTP to have that played so that you can put questions to the witness. Good morning, Mr. Poparic. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. We did some puzzles over the last 20 minutes, but Mr. Lukic will now put further questions to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First, I don't know if we can get that help from Ms. Stewart, if she can play that one or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We could that but we need to know from where what the time code is of what my friend would like played.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The time code is 8 minutes, 57 seconds up to 9 minute, 15 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps -- I take it that you want the witness to have a look at a video that will now be played, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you carefully watch your screen and look at a video that will start in a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But before we play the video, can we see on our screens in the e-court P7611, please. It's on our screens. We need page 8 in B/C/S, at least. It's not what I have in e-court as page 8. I just checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: B/C/S in e-court, page 8, is the cover page of the photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we looking at the right document, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I need P07617.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, it is stated in the document that it is a photo file created for the incident which took place at Zavnobih square.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Witness, is this the first time you see this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see this document for the first time in this format. I did have a copy, but nothing could be seen in it. The initial photographs I was able to view were received from the witness I mentioned yesterday. I did have a copy previously which was too poor to be able to see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So on this first photograph following the cover page, we can see that it says, "photo 1: Zavnobih Trg," where the shell fell?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we see the concrete slabs.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will next show you a video with Ms. Stewart's assistance. We'll have a look at 1D05911, starting with 8:57 and ending at 9:15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... tell Ms. Stewart to stop the video. And can we start, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, have you seen this video previously?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I also took a still from it which I included in my report. If it is useful, I can indicate it for you. It is photograph 14 of page 309 in the B/C/S. It is very similar to this particular still. It is the classroom where the children and the teacher were injured and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The lighter part of the picture at the top, what is it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, conditionally put, it is a window. There were boards against the wall but not all the way up to the ceiling so as to leave some daylight. On the side we can see the board full of shrapnel holes, the shrapnel killed and injured three children and the teacher.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness kindly repeat his very last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your last sentence was not heard.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shrapnel that flew through the boards injured or killed three children and the teacher and one child was hurt while being outside the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the record, we are looking at the still at 09:00.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you said these are the shrapnel holes, you are pointing at the small white dots or dots to the upper left side of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is light coming through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the wall, when we keep viewing it, we'll see some small holes. What are they in this still?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are shrapnel holes on the boards placed against the windows. These premises used to be shops before the war and these used to be shop windows. Some boards were put against them during the war, some of them were concrete, but elsewhere they were made of tin, actually, such as the type of tin used in construction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where we see the shrapnel holes, what kind of boarding could that have been? Could there have been concrete slabs outside?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were concrete and tin slabs outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the part where the shrapnel flew through?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that part there were only tin boards because shrapnel could not go through concrete. If we look at some other photographs showing the concrete obstacles, they are some 20 centimetres thick. The tin boards on the other hand, were brought in and it was the -- of the construction type. The shrapnel could have not gone through the concrete slabs and even if had gone through there would have large pieces of concrete strewn about, because concrete as a rule is brittle and no small holes could be made in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, what you're now describing was that still there when you visited the place or is it on the basis of the documentation that you draw these conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This room was changed, and I'm saying all this based on the footage and photographs I used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the details about the tin is to be found in the documentation? Because you said it's this type of tin which is used for construction, et cetera. Is that -- what's your basis of knowledge for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can see what these sheets look like. They're provided in image 11 of the report. I had the occasion to see them at construction sites. They're made of tin, and sometimes they're made of plywood, which is water-resistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I do understand that. But how were you able to what you saw on construction sites to say, Well, this is exactly the same as what was there at the time of the incident. That's my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I made the conclusion based on the dimensions and the way it looks. It is clear in my mind that that is it. It can't be anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we play further this video, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we play even further, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we stop now. Thank you. We stopped at 9 minutes, 38 seconds, .9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your view, what can we see on this video?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the video, we can see the area in front of the room moved westwards to a certain extent. It is image number 1 from the photo file that can be compared to the still we see. However, that is not the room where the students were. If we were to move towards the camera, we would come across another room at the very corner of the building where the classroom was. This is the place that the police indicated as the explosion site. It is not in dispute because we see explosion traces and shrapnel traces on the thick concrete slabs, which are about 20 centimetres thick. Behind those slabs were some 35 children, according to the police report, who luckily went unhurt. What I'm trying to say is that these slabs provided full protection against shrapnel. There were 35 children, 1st graders, there waiting for the period to end so as to enter the classroom. Had such slabs been placed against the classroom, no one would have been hurt inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we go back -- and I would tender this video, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'm afraid that you'll have to invite Ms. Stewart as well to make an excerpt, the one you played, that will put on a disk that Ms. Stewart will then give it to Madam Registrar but a number could be reserved I would say.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1340, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is reserved for an excerpt of a video as it was played a minute ago. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And just way of a description for the record, this is an excerpt from a video regarding incidents of shelling and sniping civilians in Sarajevo received from the State Commission for the Gathering of Facts on War Crimes in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That certainly will help to give a description of this -- what will be an exhibit. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now can we go back to P7617. Yeah, we need this page which is in front of us. It's page 9 in B/C/S, where the picture is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, in your view, is this the place of explosion the same where the small holes were seen in the video?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained already it's impossible. Here there were first graders who were unscathed and an explosion did happen here. You can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So how many explosions were there?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, two. I find from this video that there were two explosions. It is completely consistent with the situation that reigned at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with the incident. I should now like to go back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the first graders, we find them exactly where? In the documentation, I mean.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, in image number 11 is a broader view of the scene. In my report, I mean. It's a broader view of the scene where you can see the place of explosion and this manhole, and a close-up of the same is on image 16, a close-up based on which I was able to determine the direction. And on image 15 is the place where the classroom was, where a wreath was hung, and that corresponds to image 11. It's the same place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we briefly go and look at those images. We need the -- what's the number again of the report of the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Image 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... D1330.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 308 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I repeat: D1330.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Picture 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that again the classroom incident, picture 11?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. This is the place where the classroom was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because that's the picture we see in the other photo documentation. But I'm still ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can point out on this photograph something that's important. This drain, here, next to the light point, it's the place of the explosion, and next to the light point is the rain-water drain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And on picture 16, we can see both the drain and the place of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the -- I think the real issue is whether these are photographs taken from the same incident, yes or no. That's the basic question. But apparently you are convinced that they are. We'll have a closer look at it. Meanwhile, Mr. Lukic, you may put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it can be of assistance ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You best assist us by waiting for the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you wanted to say something very brief, tell us what you meant. You said you had something --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to say if it's of any assistance, there's also picture 15 which shows the place where the classroom was, and you see it as it was after the war when a wreath was hung there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's now move from the Zavnobih square. Yesterday we discussed incident F-5. We showed where Mr. Van der Weijden took his measurements and where Ramiza Kundo was standing. In the video, you even see her with Mr. Hogan. I don't want to go through it again. Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You marked the photograph which is now D1339 approximately the positions of the BH army and the VRS. From the place where Mr. Van der Weijden did his analysis, which is below the position of Mrs. Kundo, was he able to see the positions of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the place where he was, he couldn't see them. And whoever looks at that report could be misled into thinking that from the place of the incident you can't see the territory controlled by the BH army because the place of the incident was above and the wall is below and the wall does not obstruct the view, which means, Mr. Van der Weijden was determining visibility not at the place of the incident but from where the wall was, from the direction of the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If he had done it from the place of the incident, would he have been able to see the positions of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the position -- from the place of the incident, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I must confess that I can't follow at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you explain how do you know where Mr. Van der Weijden was --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- when he established the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we saw -- [Overlapping speakers] ... can we see P1130, page 32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And can you now answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we agreed that this can be broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We could use the public redacted version that I've given the 65 ter number of a few times now. And if it is at all helpful, I'll give it again. It's 28541B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which avoids whatever risk that there's anything shown which should not be shown.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were just discussing this photograph. We see here how Mr. Van der Weijden determined visibility from the territory controlled by the VRS, but the place of the incident wasn't here. It was, in my estimate, at least 15 metres above this point and from that place, you can see the territory. I marked it yesterday. But looking from this point, we cannot see anything to the left, and that's where the territory controlled by the BH army was. Even a bit ahead of this wall you can see from the place of the incident, but the place of the incident was not strictly defined so we can say, yes, both, there is a view or -- and there isn't a view. But over the wall you can certainly see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. But, again, you say: This photograph depicts where Mr. Van der Weijden was, but the place of the incident was somewhere else, 15 metres away. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we know that from the testimony of Mrs. Kundo and the video of Mr. Lynden. She showed that place and it's in the report. We saw it yesterday. I marked that photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Exactly that was what I was asking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... some things from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one other follow-up question. We, yesterday, looked -- also in your report, we looked at Google Earth picture where there is a lot of houses which would possibly obstruct the view further to the left of this wall. What's your opinion about those houses? Could they have obstructed the view in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time of the incident, no. The Google Earth image - and we have to bear that in mind - started posting these images in 2001 or 2003, I can't remember. And I don't know to be honest from which time this image dates. Now, for instance, there is a four-storey house there and now there is no visibility, but in the 2001 images taken by Mr. Hogan or somebody around him, there are no houses there. Now if you were to go there, the situation is different. The area has been developed. There are houses. And now on Google Earth you can see these houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How the situation exactly was in -- contemporaneously, you do not know, you can look at --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time -- I know how it was in 2001. That means six years later. At that time, there were no obstacles to visibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- which means that in 1993, there were none either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless there have been buildings which were torn down, isn't it? It's a loose conclusion. It may be right, it may be wrong, but there's no proper basis for such a conclusion, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no indication whatsoever that a house was demolished in that area. In 2001, there was nothing there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no indication that there was a house demolished. There's also no indication that there was no house demolished, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, there is no such indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, it's almost impossible to draw any conclusions. Your conclusion may be right or wrong. I'm not contesting that. But I'm testing the basis for your conclusions. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were reading the statements of Mrs. Kundo and watching the video made by Mr. Hogan, did anybody ever indicate or suggest that there had been a house that was demolished there?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was just one woman saying that there was damage to the houses, that the roof tiles had fallen off, that they had to do repairs. That's the extent of the damage. Nobody ever mentioned that in her immediate vicinity a house was demolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a name but it's not on the record.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Rasema Menzilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see P7594 shortly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we are waiting, on our transcript, 40615, it was put to you that this document includes things from medical reports. Did you see autopsy reports for the victims?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All I was able to see were excerpts from autopsy reports, for instance, a sentence: Killed by an explosion, et cetera. There were no details of the autopsies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you find in that documentation how it was established that gun-fire injuries were, in fact, inflicted by sniper?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. And I don't know how it could possibly be established if it was a sniper or not. One can only establish that it was an infantry weapon or a -- or an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the incident F-17, you remember Tarik Zunic said he was injured by a machine-gun. He recognised it.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said a light machine-gun, which is not an infantry weapon. It's a complete opposite to the sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation to finish. My waiting doesn't mean that I'm unhappy with your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was noted about Tarik Zunic? How was he injured?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was said he was hit by a sniper, but we would need to check. In fact, all these incidents are considered here as sniping incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Regarding F-6, it was put to you on transcript page 40626 that -- I'll read it in English from line 4: "[In English] And you also agree that there is a clear unobstructed line of sight between the place of the incident and the Orthodox church in Veljine; right? "A. Yes." [Interpretation] Can you tell us what is characteristic about this particular place of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is characteristic is that the whole length of the bridge metal -- a metal barrier, 2.5 metres high, was set up. One could not see the cars passing. There was only a stretch of about 5, 6 metres of visibility towards the church at Veljine and that photograph was marked by Mrs. Sanija Dzevlah, and it's in image 19 in my report. So the whole bridge was not completely open towards the church at Veljine. It had a protective barrier made of steel slabs, 2.5 metres high. Only in a narrow stretch was there a view, and I confirmed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see it's time [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's break time. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom. Perhaps we could use the time in relation to P6970. On the 2nd of December in 2014 during the testimony of Milorad Sajic, a military diary was marked for identification as P6970. On the 7th of October, 2015, the Prosecution informed the Defence and the Chamber that it had uploaded an extract of this diary under Rule 65 ter number 8656D. Having heard of no objection from the Defence, the Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to assign the extract to P6970, and admitted P6970 into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have 1D5677 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While waiting for the document, I just wanted to have something recorded in the transcript. It has to do with the incident F-6. My learned friend Ms. Edgerton, at transcript page 40627, put to you that the witness never said that she was visiting her mother and that it was stated by the Prosecutor in error. Let us look at page 7 of this document in e-court. It should correspond to transcript page 3518, starting with line 19, I will read out this part. [In English] I quote: "Q. You have testified that you had visited your mother at the hospital and you were on your way back. I presume you were on your ... back home. "A. Yes." [Interpretation] Did you bear this part of her testimony in mind.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I quoted it in my report. I did not follow this discussion in the further than that. I was simply interested in learning whether it was possible for her to be there at 4.30 p.m. as she had stated in her first statement. It is irrelevant whether she was visiting her mother or not. I was just trying to establish whether the time indicated would fit with her initial statement where she said that it was at 4.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you, you drew more or less conclusions from the fact that patients could not be visited apart from at certain times. So if you say it's irrelevant, you did put some weight on visiting the mother rather than fetching medication. I'm just giving you an opportunity to explain what I consider to be not fully consistent, that it's irrelevant, and, at the same time, you draw -- you pay attention to it and even draw, to some extent, conclusions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think we understood each other well. Mrs. Kundo, in her first statement, said that the incident took place at half past 4.00. Then in another statement, she repeated that she left her home at around 3.00 p.m. and headed towards the hospital. Later on she said that she was there to visit her mother but changed the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm -- you're not addressing the point I raised. You have an opportunity to do so. If not, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And if I may, Your Honours, if at page 24, line 8, there is some inference that I might have been making a false representation, I feel I need to rise on that and invite my friend to identify that portion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- could we leave that until after I have received an answer from the witness. So I gave you another opportunity to address the matter and -- otherwise we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try. In the report, I made reference to both times and I only relied on the statement to check whether it was possible for her if she had left whom at 3.00 and if she was indeed visiting her mother to be able to be at that location at half past 4.00. That was my only interest, to see whether it was possible at all for her to be there if she had left her home at 3.00, and bearing in mind the distance to the hospital. I was trying to assess whether she could be there at that time. That's all. That was why I used this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least in one of the options visiting hours played a role, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She came at that time and was held back a bit ... and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have now 1D05675 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are about to see a statement, the statement of this witness. There, we see she says as follows: "On 6 January 1994 around 1630 hours, I was coming home by bicycle." Is that the statement you just referenced?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is her initial statement from back in 1993 or 1994 where she specified the time of 4.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that the statement was provided on the 30th of September, 1994. In the signature block, we see her signature.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see her signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And a date in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 1995. But this was probably affixed later after she had reviewed some document. The statement itself was taken on the 30th of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would offer this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1D05675 receives exhibit number D1341, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. I now address the matter raised by Ms. Edgerton. Mr. Lukic, you said: "My learned friend Ms. Edgerton put to you that the witness never said that she was visiting her mother." That's not what Ms. Edgerton did. If you look at the relevant pages that is 40627 and 628 -- sorry Mr. Lukic. Yes. Ms. Edgerton read to the witness portion of a transcript in which it clearly is stated that earlier the witness had said this, and whether she now still says the same. So that the witness had never said that is not what Ms. Edgerton put to the witness. She put to the witness whether the witness had ignored that the then witness had corrected her statement during the testimony upon questions put to her by Judge El Mahdi. That's the situation and let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I just direct your attention, Your Honour, to line 2 of page 40627: "Q. Let's just focus on your assertion about her visiting her mother. She never said she was visiting her mother."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I overlooked that. Later, however, what she read clearly indicates that she accepts that the witness said that once, having drawn my attention now to line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- 2, Ms. Edgerton, I think Mr. Lukic is right, that if you said that she never said that is certainly inconsistent with what you put later to the witness. How inappropriate it is, is still to be considered. I mean, it is apparently is not a way of confusing the witness, because later it was laid out very well. Nevertheless, Ms. Edgerton, if you use your own words to introduce these matters, if you'd be a bit more cautious in what words you use, that certainly would assist both the witness and the Chamber and would save Mr. Lukic some emotional responses. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Happens from time to time. Thank you, Your Honour. I would move on to incident F-2 now. And if we can have P07598 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting for it, at transcript page 40627, lines 7 to 13, my learned friend told you that the photograph shown to you -- perhaps I did not cite the right page. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next one. Can we have page 2 from this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She put to you that there was an unobstructed visibility from Spicasta Stijena and the location of the incident. You said that it was not the case and you were stopped. You were not allowed to continue. Please explain to us briefly whether you wanted to add something.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to add about something that we can see here. I wanted to dispute the assertion that VRS positions at Spicasta Stijena are visible. First of all, this photograph, in my view, was taken by a person standing in front of the house where the victim had stood. In the photograph you have shown, there was a crossed-out area and it represents a room added on to later. When Mr. Hogan was there one could see that there was a door. It would have been fair to take a photograph so that the door is visible and that the direction is known. In my report, in image 57, I show that these were not VRS positions. I was able to do so because the last roof -- the last trench at Spicasta Stijena is clearly visible. It was a large trench and some parts of it remain. I visited the area personally and as I explained in examination-in-chief I measured the distance between the warring parties. We can also see the footage involving the Black Swans that has been shown in the courtroom. Based on all that, I concluded that the VRS positions were slightly to the right from the last point of the roof that we can see. So to the right. That is where the VRS positions were. I claim that in this photograph we cannot see the place where VRS positions were, and I showed that in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... having consulted my colleagues, Mr. Lukic, I am going to stop what happens here. What happens is you've introduced a report in which approximately 60 per cent of the materials are not directly related to the expertise of this witness. He assumes, he compares statements, he says what he has seen, what he hasn't seen, he evaluates the evidence, et cetera, it's only missing that he also tells us that he is writing the Judgement for us. That is not -- and what this has triggered that the Prosecution, perhaps understandably, paid a lot of attention to that as well, which perhaps for reasons of testing credibility and reliability is something the Prosecution would have to do. Now, in re-examination, we just continue with that. Again, the whole of the evaluation of the evidence, that's -- Mr. Lukic, limit your questions which you've failed to do in reviewing the report already, limit your questions to the expertise of this witness, and that is not what he's talking about 80 per cent of his time. Please keep this in mind. We're not going to continue like this. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. But if I may, please, if Mr. Van der Weijden as the OTP expert witness discussed the same issue, our position is that we can rebut and refute his claims through our expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To some extent, it's right. To some extent, it's not, because this witness goes far, far further than Mr. Van der Weijden does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Van der Weijden exactly pointed out here that there were Serb positions visible and Mr. Poparic checked and found that it's not true, so we have to address this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... this is perhaps an example where you are more right, but weighing what A, B, C and D said and again, let me be quite clear to you the testimony of Mr. Van der Weijden is, indeed, has some flaws in this respect as well and that was not remain -- that did not remain unnoticed by the Chamber. Let me leave it to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What I'd just like to underscore is that this incident was not a charged incident in this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's another matter that -- but, again, just as I -- the Chamber accepts, to some extent, that by testing the Unscheduled Incidents, if there was serious flaws in evidence presented by the Prosecution, if testing that evidence could shed additional light on reliability and credibility of the OTP witnesses, the Chamber has allowed you to do that. We never said you should not deal with this one. That is certainly not where we have drawn the line. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now move -- P07599?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we have to go to the private session for a short period of time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I need D01330 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, it's your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I need page 59 in English version only.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution showed you one document which is now P01007. In fact, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can that be broadcast, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought to skip that, I don't have time I just mention it. And actually the picture number is P07595, where Mr. Djozo marked where the wood that was cut down was in relation to Spicasta Stijena, and I wanted to ask Mr. Poparic something based on this photo which is on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Poparic, you see before you image 32 from your report. Who took this photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I need help of the usher so Mr. Poparic can mark something, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, could you mark the young woods that had been cut during the war?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it stretches over to the left which you can't see in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in relation to Spicasta Stijena, where is it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is below a bit to the left or shall we say to the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would offer this, if we can make a photo out of this screen and I would propose it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, screen shot marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives exhibit number D1342, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But we still need to have it ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness: Do you see the house where the person was shot? The location of the incident.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It's not the photograph that relates to. It's the photograph where those seven forests are marked but it's from another angle, so it wasn't clear which forest it is relative to Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This forest is much larger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think that it needs to be under seal, this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we -- Madam Registrar, it's admitted not under seal but as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, very briefly about incident F-17 where Tarik Zunic was injured on 16 March 1995. You don't have to go to that page in your report. I'm just going to ask you: Could that place be seen from Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a view. It's not a very good view but ... we didn't deal with it in great detail, but there is visibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you about incident 9 in Djordja Andrejevica Kuna Street number 7 from 15 May 1995. It's in your report, page 346 in English; and B/C/S, 327. After that, you were shown one document. First of all, my colleague showed you, on transcript page 40676 from lines 4 to 12, and she said she saw no reference to the school for the blind in this document. She asked if that is true. You said yes. And I'd like to see that document again, which received number P07600. In the second paragraph, it says: "On 15 May 1995 around 1730, this SJB received information from the third police station of the same SJB that in Nerkez Smailagic Street number 10, citizen Stevan Bjelac had been wounded by a sniper shot fired from the aggressor's positions in Nedzarici." What place do you think was designated in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the aggressor's position in Nedzarici? Those were positions around the school for the blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why do you think Nedzarici so? Nedzarici is a large area.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, but the school for the blind is also there and it's the most forward Serb position relative to this location of the incident. Other positions, it's pointless to consider them, because they were all obstructed by buildings. The only position possible was the school for the blind and that's what the police noted. It was only possible from there, impossible from other positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure if this document is uploaded, 1D05937. [In English] Can we see it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how well you can see it; but could you, on this map, with the usher's assistance, mark the co-ordinates. The first is 859 and the second is 578. So 859 and 578.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not writing. Shall I draw lines to make it clearer? So at the intersection of these two lines -- let me try again. Let me just check. 859?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And 578.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it, at the intersection of these two lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The problem is I can't see any intersection of lines.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll mark it with a 1. Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mean this point?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let it be number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where is that location?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a bit to the north from the school for the blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you put a circle around the school for the blind and mark it with number 2.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we -- we would offer this document into exhibits -- exhibit -- as marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives exhibit number D1343, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Just to make everything perfectly clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the highest-up marking looks like a letter L, more or less, and it is exactly at the corner of that L that the witness, I think, marked number 1, so where the two lines are crossing, whereas, in the circle, he marked where the school of the blind is. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll skip two incidents. Let us focus on F-7 of 25 May 1994. In B/C/S, it's page 151 in your report; in English, it's 153. We won't dwell on it, but you know that it was put to you here that there were weapons of 120 millimetres, there was one Praga there, and you told us that you investigated only infantry weapons. Do you remember now which type of weapons was dealt with by the Prosecution expert, Mr. Van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He also dealt only with infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No cannons or Pragas?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were shown image 105 from your report. In B/C/S, it's 148; and in English, it's 150. On transcript page 40742 - 40742 - it was said by my learned friend that there are absolutely no trees blocking the line of sight from the theological faculty, so I should like to show now a photograph, the same one shown by my learned friend, P07610.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 10 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see the photograph on our screens. As for the two sides we can see in front of us on the photograph, can one hit the bus that was at the intersection at Nikola Demonja and Bulevar Avnoja?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the firing positions we can see here, it was not possible. It covers the angle between south-east and south-west in the direction of Alipasino Polje and Vojnicko Polje, whereas Dobrinja is in the direction of south-east or south-west. That is where Dobrinja is, so to the left of this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask the assistance of the usher so I would ask Mr. Poparic to mark something on this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the extent possible, please, mark the location where the tree was that we can see in photograph 106 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in front of the large building on the other side. This is the only way I can indicate it, if it helps any. If we stood on the opposite side from the side we see here, on the right-hand side of the right-hand side building, then we would be able to see the tree, and we would be looking in the direction of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would offer this marked picture into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives exhibit number D1344, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Let me just try to fully understand. Are you saying -- you mean from the firing positions here. Do you mean that are these the firing positions in that wall, it is relatively dark, black, one hole, and one, more or less, a line, apparently. Is that what you had on your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The wall was broken through and probably a firing position was arranged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's a probability. What about any firing positions at the side of the building we cannot see at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I said that I reviewed the photographs and there are no such firing positions, except on this side and on the opposite side, the far end. There, there are also some firing positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But whether they would have fired through windows they could open or whether at not the far end but at the long end of the other side, whether there would have been any possible firing positions, you wouldn't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot know that and I have no such evidence. What I could see is what I registered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were shown P07611. I'll be brief about it. You were shown page 13 in the B/C/S and 14 in the English version. My learned friend started with the 4th of September, 1993, specifying the wounded. There is mention made of the Sanac settlement. Where is it located in terms of the warring parties' positions?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a reference to the Sanac settlement and Sremska. It is all part of Sremska Street, with some small streets around it. The settlement itself is called Sanac. That settlement is at Hrasno Brdo overlooking the stadium at Grbavica but below Ozrenska Street and there were separation lines there practically. The Sanac settlement was controlled by the ABiH. It is in the immediate vicinity of the Grbavica stadium and Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then you were taken to the 6th of September where Topal Osman Pasa street number 20 is referenced.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is its current name whereas before it was called Milutina Djuraskovica. That street takes you from the Grbavica stadium to Elektroprivreda.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the warring parties' positions?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If looking from the Grbavica stadium towards Elektroprivreda, on the left-hand side of the street there was ABiH-controlled territory to the west, whereas the eastern or right side was Grbavica, i.e., VRS-controlled territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the Prosecution expert Mr. Van der Weijden investigated any other cases of wounding in the area?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I remember he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he investigate any other cases that go beyond the scope of the indictment or of your report?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me briefly -- no, let's stay with F-4. Something about Ozrenska Street. At transcript page -- you don't have it in your report. At transcript page 40755, in line 20, you explained where the photographs were taken, and you said: "I dispute that the photograph was taken by Mr. Van der Weijden from that spot." In my view, you did not mention the spot you had in mind. What is the spot that you think Mr. Van der Weijden did not take the photograph from?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the place he indicated, which is at 829 metres from the place of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us next look at P --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This should not be broadcasted. 01130 which is Mr. Van der Weijden's report. We need page 32 only in English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For ease of reference it is image 74 of your report, at page 106 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: This can be broadcast if we used 65 ter number 28541B, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But then we can be confused later when we review the evidence from the case because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment I suggest to do at the same time we note that this picture doesn't hurt. So let's continue rather than to start a battle over that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sure. And I apologise, I probably misspoke. I need page 25 in English version from this document. That also can be broadcast. First, can we see middle -- picture in the middle of the page, please, enlarged with the title above it. In the middle of the page with the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, you were asked about the co-ordinates and who used what. Did Mr. Van der Weijden make a link between the co-ordinates and the place from which the bullet was fired?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this case, he said that these were the co-ordinates, specifying that it is some 829 metres away from the place of the incident, as we can see it in this image at the end of this yellow building. That is where the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see -- hmm. I'm trying to calculate ... can we go three pages back, please, from this point. So page 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we still safe as far as broadcast is concerned, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think so. We -- but.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's take no risk. Then please refer to the redacted version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Can we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton knows that number by heart. Ms. Edgerton, it was ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's the 65 ter number. Could we have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if you can see it in this page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... B/C/S version, I'm sorry. I cannot locate it. Aside from English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, has the public redacted version also a B/C/S translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need page 29 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S, towards the middle, it says: "The alleged position."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English translation, it is the alleged shooting position. That what was going to ask you about. The alleged shooting position from which fire was opened in Ozrenska Street, and then we have the co-ordinates. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And distance to incident site: 829 metres.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you recall, did Mr. Van der Weijden provide a photograph from the alleged shooting position?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did provide a photograph of that building at 829 metres, according to his assertion, and we viewed it during examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Stop there. Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we go back to D01330, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S, it is page 109. [In English] And if we -- I cannot locate it in -- there it is. It's page 108 in English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What can we see here?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this photograph, the lower one, is the one provided by Mr. Van der Weijden from the distance of 829 metres. He marked in the little square in the photograph the house at that distance as specified in the previous paragraph as the place of firing. But the house is not at the distance of 829 metres. It is some 600 metres away in ABiH-controlled territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the position at 829 metres marked by the co-ordinates, in whose territory is that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in Ozrenska Street, just above the pavement in that street. It corresponds approximately to the positions where VRS trenches were. They were slightly below but, more or less, that would be the location. However, it would not be the location as marked here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see it's a break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is. Witness, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, as matters stand now, could you give us any idea on how much more time you'd need once re-examination is concluded?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Think very moment, my estimate would be 30 minutes. Subject to what might come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, could you try to conclude in such a way that 30 minutes would be left or at least 20-plus minutes would be left for Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I quickly raise one matter that was alluded to yesterday, Mr. President. That was the submission of the table that we discussed at the end of the day and discussed timing on that. We're prepared to send that to the Trial Chamber right now. I discussed it with Mr. Lukic. Obviously he's not in a position to review it now so we consider that the best expedient would be to handle it in the same way the analogous table was handled with expert Subotic, and that was provided the court sees they are appropriate, they be admitted and then he have several days or a week to review it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, always appreciated if the parties agree on something. No problems as far as the Chamber is concerned. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now something about incident F-8. That's 14 June 1994. You don't need to open the report. It was a tram along the Zmaja od Bosne Street. You were asked about the Jewish cemetery, and you were shown P00077. That's a video. Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we now see photograph 112 from your report, D01330, image 112.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S ... in English it's 158, and it's enough if we see only English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your report, we have a similar photograph under number 110 taken by Mr. Hogan, but we'll work with this one. Who took this photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From where was it taken?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was taken approximately from the place the witness claimed the tram was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... usher now. We have to mark something on this, this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, first of all, could you mark - if you know and if can you see it - the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very small, but I recognise -- I'll put a circle around it. To me it's a landmark. This little chapel, it's the entrance to the Jewish cemetery, and ahead of it and above is the Jewish cemetery. Maybe this perspective is not the best.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What do you think is the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the chapel?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1 on the chapel; and the rest marked by 2.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, can you mark the trench or the bunker where we -- which we saw on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only mark the approximate direction from which it is seen. That's where the trench was. Shall I put number 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you now mark Debelo Brdo. But before do you that, which forces were there at Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark here the territory controlled by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The separation line stretched in this direction, downwards. I cannot mark it precisely. At Grbavica after Miljacka, and then from the Jewish cemetery, here. You can't see it in the picture, it's in the background where there were positions of the VRS. I'm trying to mark behind this forest at Zlatiste, I can't mark it precisely, it's all green. At Zlatiste, were the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska and all this, this was the city, was controlled by the BH army. I can mark it with 4. Debelo Brdo shall be 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So 4 and 5 were under the control of who?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would offer this into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives exhibit number D1345, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can I ask a follow-up question to that. You marked 4 and 5 on two sides of the separation line. And you say both are BH-held territory? 4 and 5; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But the separation line in between two areas held by the BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But number 5 I marked Debelo Brdo. It's a bit at the top. You can't see it very well from the forest. It was around there. That's where BH army positions were and behind them were the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. 5 was just supposed to denote where, approximately, Debelo Brdo was. Is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, you should have put the 5 a little bit below the separation line; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could have. I wasn't thinking about that. Maybe I should mark it with a dot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's sufficient. You have clarified that matter and now I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, may I take it that the Chamber is better served by orienting itself on the maps because this inherently is inaccurate.
