I mean, to draw a line somewhere between some trees, there's no way that it could add to what is more accurate that is, what we find in the various maps were the confrontation lines where, of course, is clearly stated where Debelo Brdo is, where Zlatiste is because it's not from the left to the right, it goes a bit further, a bit further back. But let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't prepare the map so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. But that, perhaps, better assists us. I had not said yet, which I should have done, that D1345 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And thank you to Judge Fluegge for clarifying the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to look at a photograph that was perhaps a bit confusing. It's incident F-10. [In English] And we need your document, which is D01330. And we need only English version, page 180.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That shouldn't be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked, Mr. Poparic, about this liquid. You said it was water.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you conclude it was water, not blood?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on two facts. This surface, you see how large it is? And considering that the victim had sustained a relatively small injury to the tissue, he couldn't have bled so much. He was immediately transported to the hospital. And the other thing is that, at the right corner of this stain, there is a mirror.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this witness telling us what kind of [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... why he thinks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we're not interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not interested in quasi-expertise where the witness is not an expert, and we first listen to his answer and then he says something about injuries and that slight injury, he could not have bled, that requires expert evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will move on. I was just felt obliged because he was questioned on this issue. If he does not have anything to say on it, I will gladly move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Then we can move to open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open -- we were in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, we were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Ms. Edgerton, I think, kindly drew your attention to the fact that the picture should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing more, nothing less.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We were not in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask to have D01330 or our screens again, please. And we just need page 162 in English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On transcript page related to this photograph - that's page 40795 - my colleague asked you at line 25 and straddling the next page until line 4, the following question: "Did you investigate the hole in the tin?" In fact, you did not do that. You based your opinion on the photograph, and you confirmed?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were reading the report of Mr. Van der Weijden, the Prosecution expert, did you determine whether Mr. Van der Weijden examined the hole in the tin sheet or he, too, used only the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't investigate the hole either. He couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why do you think he couldn't?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was many years after the incident. That item was not available anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were also asked -- in fact, it was put to you on T.40797 that you did not examine the material either.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Reading the report of Mr. Van der Weijden, did you find that he had examined the material?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you something about materials and Honourable Judge Fluegge asked the same thing. You were asked about the homogeneity of materials. You told us yesterday that he were a mechanical engineer by training. In your career, did you have any contact with tin sheets and quality control of tin sheets?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In what capacity?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I dealt with construction and I prescribed in my technical drawings the material and it was often tin, so I had to provide a specification for that tin and the quality control necessary. In the production, everything is standardized, from manufacturing to quality control. It's a highly controlled product.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are there control standards in place?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. All over the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with them?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mention some of such steel control standards now.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the standard numbers but I can tell you what they deal with. First of all, there is control of chemical quality then a separate standard for the control of mechanical characteristics as well as standard to control the technological characteristics, or technical characteristics. If you have some technology retirements that have to do with the way steel is manufactured, such controls are also in place so that the product contains appropriate characteristics; for example, in the case of nuts and bolts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us move onto another topic. We'll talk about the dust cloud which appeared after a shot was fired. At transcript page 40803, from line 13 to 15, it was put to you that in the Karadzic case you accepted that the analysis of the dust cloud was not based on any published papers or studies. In your response, you said that general principles apply, in terms of the strike theory. However, I would like to ask you the following today. Where can we find these general principles of the strike theory?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The strike theory can be found in any significant textbook for mechanical engineering as studied at universities. It was also something I studied in the course of my studies in quite some detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We are now moving quickly to a different subject. That's incident F-11. And let's look at image 147.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can have only English version. It's page 202.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to refresh your memory about what you discussed with my learned friend, Ms. Edgerton. You were asked if you had investigated whether the wounded person had moved in this case, whether he was changing position. You explained that you were collecting material evidence. And my question only to you regarding this incident is this: Do you remember whether in his report, Mr. Van der Weijden, the Prosecution expert, had investigated the possibility that this man had moved.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not investigate anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now F-14. And in the indictment, it's F-13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need image 164. In B/C/S, it's page 218, but we need on the screen page 228 in English on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's just to refresh your memory about the incident. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My colleague put to you on page T.40288 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry. Maybe I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 40828. She asked you if you agreed - at line 15 - that in the Karadzic case you had agreed it had not been measured in the official report what the vertical distance was of the entry and exit wound in the man's arm, and you agreed there was just a general description.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember today when Mr. Van der Weijden examined the same incident, did he measure that vertical distance and did he put it in his report?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please bear with me. Can we have on our screens, 1D00691.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My friend asked you yesterday about determination [Realtime transcript read in error "the termination"] of the scene of incident based on Palo, Huso's statement. He provided the statement on the 23rd November 1994 about the incident of the day before. Actually, he provided a statement on the 24th and the incident took place on the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic did you say the witness was asked about the determination of the scene? I'm only asking because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Statements were shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm only asking you because you are recorded as having said, "the termination" and I think you said "determination."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Determination. Should be determination. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that statement is actually marked for identification already. It's a Defence exhibit D1336.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate help from my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Palo on -- says that on the 23rd of November, 1994, he was driving the tram garage number 263. At 1535 hours, he was heading towards Marin Dvor and Remiza. What is Remiza?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a tram garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on that, were you able to determine the direction from Marin Dvor towards Remiza?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He goes on to say: "And when I reached the section between the technical school and the Marsal Tito barracks, specifically the turning towards the new railway station, I heard a sound of something hitting the tram as if someone had thrown a stone at it." Do you know where the turning point is?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what about the photograph you marked?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is photograph 164. Somewhere towards the front of the ellipsis where we see the words "tram 236," that is where the turning is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if it ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So can we go back now to D01330, back to that image. We need ... we need page, only in English version, 228, please. Can we enlarge this image 164, please. Can we have help of the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, using this photograph, can you mark the position between the technical school and the Marsal Tito barracks at the turning.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now that the photograph is enlarged, I can see that the turning should be approximately where the letter T is. It means that the tram had already turned to the west, towards the station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The letter T meaning?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tram 263 ^ [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it says tram. Approximately this is where the turning should be in the photograph, just before the bend itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where is that location in relation to the two museums?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in between. One museum is marked with the number 3; the other with the number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm a bit puzzled where you had said: "It had turned already to the west ..." Could you then -- because I do understand that west on this picture is to the left. It came from Marin Dvor. Where has this tram turned to the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I did not express myself well. It actually kept going straight. It was moving from Marin Dvor and went past the turning. He didn't turn right towards the train station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what makes you believe that if you read the description that it would be where the T is now and not, for example, at the middle of that T-junction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The turning is just before the intersection. The road to the train station is to the right so it needs to turn in the intersection, but before the intersection, it needs to assume its position, or, actually, move along the railings that make it turn geometrically. The turning must before the intersection itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That depends on the interpretation of what you consider to be a turning point, when the turning is complete, or when you start the turning, or when you're halfway the turning. Isn't it true that this is rather interpretation used by a witness rather than anything you were -- that your expertise could tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is just a piece of information that I took into consideration to analyse the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In our language the term "turning" is a technical term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see in the transcript that it is recorded that a turning is a technical term. What did you say above that -- or in addition?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a mechanical element on the rails which actually directs the train. It is controlled from the train itself. It's a mechanism, a switch. That is what I had in mind rather than a line of turning. A turning or a switch is a technical element, technical word in our language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we're began back at interpreting other evidence rather than -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to be able to do your job as the ballistics expert, and I would say it involves all of the cases, would you first need to be able to determine the location when -- where someone was wounded in order to check where the shot could have come from?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And in two cases, as far as I know, I was unsuccessful in doing so. We specified it in the report. We said that we could not assess precisely because we lacked precise information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few moments, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, this would be all we had for you. Thank you for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think the witness marked where the letter T of the tram was. He just put a dot on the T. Do you want that to be in evidence or is it clear enough that it's at the T.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but we can save this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then we'll save it. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives exhibit D1346, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Mr. Lukic, I'm -- you are aware that you could have used more time but you decided to do as you did. Ms. Edgerton, any further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And two submissions with respect to two documents that were still outstanding from the cross-examination but I could do that at the end of re-direct, one being the frame stills that I talked about last week from clips that the witness commented on and the other on P7068. But, as I said, I could do that at the end of re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, at this moment, please proceed with your re-examination -- with your --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Re-cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Re-cross, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, now in your redirect examination incidents, we've discussed incidents F-2, F-6, F-7, F-8, F-10 in your report. Now, those incidents weren't charged in this case but you're aware, because you testified in the Karadzic case that Mr. Van der Weijden has made a report which addressed each of these same incidents. You're aware of that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you know, for example, that in respect of incident F-2 -- oh. To help everyone, that report is 65 ter number 13574. And you know from having studied that report that in respect of incident F-2, for example, Mr. Van der Weijden provided photos showing a clear line of sight from Spicasta Stijena to the incident location and also noted that the victim had been playing outside for an hour and a half before she was shot, which contradicts your position as to line of sight. You know that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And in respect of incident F-6 which you've also discussed, you know that Mr. Van der Weijden says in his report for the Karadzic case on this incident that the victim must have been seen before getting onto the bridge, which would contradict your assertion that the shooter must have fired .99 seconds before she came in view of the Orthodox church. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it hasn't been proven --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Poparic, I asked you whether you were aware of Mr. Van der Weijden's position in his expert report in the Karadzic case relating to this incident. Could you answer the question: Were you aware?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you also know that in his report, in respect of incident F-9 -- pardon me, F-8 he visited the alleged sniping location and reported that it offered several good positions with a view to the incident site, which would tend to contradict your position that the tram was shot from the Executive Council building. You know his position, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that Mr. Van der Weijden mistakenly indicated the spot where the trams were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- before we continue like this. You have studied the report of Mr. Van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are aware that, in many respects, your conclusions differ from his opinions and conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now come to the point which you apparently would like to make, Ms. Edgerton, because the witness the whole of the report has clearly shown that his conclusions are not the same as those of Mr. Van der Weijden very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And what I would like to do, Your Honours, is ask that those sections of Mr. Van der Weijden's report in the Karadzic case dealing with these unscheduled incidents, which are not included in his report in the Mladic case, be tendered as a Prosecution Exhibit. And that would be excerpts from 65 ter number 13574 which we would upload, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think I was too early, Ms. Edgerton. I missed the point that you -- one second. I missed the point that these were sections of the report which were not part of the Mladic sections. I ignored that or neglected and therefore I should not have intervened. You want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would object at this point, Your Honour, because the Prosecution should reopen the case for this, I think. If they want to introduce something else through their expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just, first of all, give an opportunity to Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I can -- if I can say one more thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why we asked our expert witnesses to address many issues in their reports is that the Prosecution already introduced documents in connection of those incidents. So we had in our case documents that address like police records for the incident that was not in our indictment. So we cannot just leave it like that. But the Prosecution does not have the right to introduce their expertise or the expertise of their expert witness in this manner. That's our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Because this is a bit systemic, I'll be happy to address it. Under normal circumstances, it would be a classical 94 bis submission, which would give rise to the tendering of documentation arising from an expert. But as we see here, the Defence has tendered evidence and proffered testimony from a purported expert, whose expertise and conclusions are subject to challenge from a variety of sources. And in this particular instance, given, in particular, the circumstances where this witness chose to address systemically the issue of campaign, the issue of the various aspects of the Prosecution's case, through the testimony of their expert who had been previously confronted with this very information in another context, and who, therefore, was well aware that in the course of forming and framing his opinions is a perfectly valid and, indeed, virtually inevitable means of testing his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, is it correct that in any case the Prosecution had in its possession the report of this witness before cross-examination began?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No question about that, Mr. President -- Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that therefore these incidents as discussed by this witness in his report, the Prosecution was aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution was aware of the positions this witness took in his report but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shouldn't the Prosecution therefore have prepared to tender Mr. Van der Weijden's evidence in the Karadzic case during the cross-examination of this witness? Rather than the re- cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, you can -- that may be better addressed for Ms. Edgerton in terms of the allocation of the time she had to address all of the potential issues raised in the report. But it's clear that was directly confronted with allegations related to these specific incidents in the course of the re-direct examination and dealt with that in a timely fashion immediately upon the conclusion of the re-direct, when we were directly confronted with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider whether it should grant the objection, yes or no. We want to take more time for that. Therefore, the -- those reports will be marked for identification and -- no, it's not -- Ms. Edgerton, you refer to it -- do we have numbers for it already? Because you referred to it only in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The report in -- the public redacted report in its entirety has been uploaded at 65 ter number 13574 and my request was for those incidents unscheduled in the present indictment, the sections related to those incidents to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore you make an excerpt. We reserve a number for it. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One matter occurs to me, Mr. President, and that's in light of the Court's remarks. I mean, there are two ways of moving through the materials. As the Court is aware, in circumstances, for example, where we have considered that tendering the difference between determining what an expert knew and asking that witness about it and obtaining information about the matters considered or not considered might be different from what one would tender. And Ms. Edgerton was moving systematically through those aspects until the point at which the Court raised its question, subsequently noting that if it had considered that it related to materials not in evidence it wouldn't have. So I just don't want to find us in a position where she was moving through a determination of what matters this expert was aware of and did or didn't consider, in contrast to the admissibility issuing which is obviously a slightly different issue. So that's a compromise position the Court can consider, permitting her to continue her re-cross-examination as it was proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said before, I intervened too early and not on a right basis. That is a matter which is -- apart -- let me just consult with my colleagues. Unless, Mr. Lukic, you'd like to add something.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to add something on the topic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- Judge Moloto just raised. Timing. The same was addressed in Karadzic report. The same issues, same topics. So it's been in Mr. Poparic's product in his work for a long time. There is nothing new. So it is -- we think that it's absolutely not appropriate to address it in re-cross. It's not that -- it's not me who raised these issues. Absolutely not me. It's been there for a long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, the parties are invited to make written submissions on the admission of these materials and we'd like to receive that within ten days from now. Further, Ms. Edgerton, you may proceed with your line of questioning, which is not in any way anticipating what our decision will be on the admission.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honours, I made my point with respect to that, and I'd just like that move on with an effort to conclude -- or in an effort to conclude before we break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which will be in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I may be able to achieve that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, in respect of P7617, page 9, you gave some evidence in your redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And I'd like to look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's not the photo that I was after. If I could just have your indulgence for a moment. There we have it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Poparic, in respect of this photograph, you said at temporary transcript page 15 -- actually you were asked: "Mr. Poparic, in your view, is this the place of explosion the same where the small holes were seen in the video?" And you said: "I explained already it's impossible. Here, there were first graders who were unscathed and an explosion did happen here. You can see that." So my question for you is: Is that the photo of the explosion of the shell that killed Mrs. Gunjic and the school children? The scene of the explosion, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpretation that I got is not really what I said but I can answer nevertheless. This is not the scene of the explosion that -- where Mrs. Gunjic was a victim.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we move into private session then, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Have we dealt with the other matters you -- we have not, but we should take a break first. Do we need the witness for that after the break? No reason to --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, although there are some administrative matters still to be dealt with, we have concluded hearing your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, for having answered the many, many questions that were put to you, both by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break. We'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00. We'll deal then with some left-overs, and we might deal briefly with a few procedural matters as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first start with any remaining matter from the testimony of the last witness. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, just very briefly, Your Honour. I just wanted to raise the frame-by-frame stills that we had made at 65 ter number 33365, hearing Your Honours' express of interest in having stills of the video that was 1D05925, which was played in court and commented on by the witness. So the matter was -- I had brought those to Your Honours at the beginning of this week and the matter was put in abeyance pending some input or review by Mr. Lukic and so that we don't lose track of those, I wonder if those could be admitted now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you give a number of this separate document? Not the number of the video but of the stills.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The stills have 65 ter number 33365.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number was incomplete on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, I see that now, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a series of 64 stills, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Actually, 46.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Six and four were right but the order was wrong. 65 ter number 33365 receives exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7619, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7619 is admitted into evidence. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And the second one was with regard to P7608, MFI, which was a document dated 11 August 1993, strictly confidential ABiH, enemy assessment - an enemy assessment was title of it - from assistant Chief of Staff for intelligence and security. Now having looked at the document, Your Honour, understanding my friend's objection to be an inability to know who wrote the document, I would submit that would only go to its weight, Your Honours. The document was manifestly prepared by the army for contemporaneous reporting purposes through the intelligence chain, and I would note is not dissimilar in content to P7609. So given this, I would think the inability to identify a particular signator would not go against its admission and ask for that to be fully admitted at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what its provenance is.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes. This was the document that had been duly authenticated from the military archives from the ABiH Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was that the document where after each and every page was such a certification included?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the issue is weight or admissibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Issue is admissibility. First of all, I would like to see that manifestly, that is manifestly visible, it's prepared by the army. It's not in the document. That's exactly why we objected. That's not at all there. Not that it's manifestly there. So there is no source and we don't who prepared it. And it's not that we objected to the content and then it's similar to something else. No. We object to admissibility because we do not know the source who prepared it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's what you wanted to submit then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will give a decision on admission or nonadmission in due course, having heard the submissions by the parties. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. President, before we move on from matters related to the recent testimony, may I raise one matter that will move things further forward, and that's with respect to the tendering of the excerpts from Mr. Van der Weijden's report in the Karadzic case, which was uploaded as 65 ter 13574. On consideration, the Prosecution would withdraw its tendering of those excerpts and simply rely on the re-cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That saves you, Mr. Lukic, also making further submissions. Any other matter in relation to the testimony of the witness which has left us half an hour ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably we will have to deal with documents mentioned in the report and we submitted our list to Madam Registrar and probably my learned friend from the opposite would -- she just provided us with a list but I really cannot comment on this, at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I take it that we have seen that list now. Table of Prosecution materials in relation to Mile Poparic. We haven't seen yours yet, and that is a -- if I can see that well, it's a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We provided updated one, since documents were admitted during the examination of Mr. Poparic. So we provided one this morning that is updated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what I would like very much the party to do as well is to consider whether there's any objection against the admission of any of those documents once they are exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the -- I was going to rise to make a distinction between those two and that my interest in doing so is further amplified by the Court's -- perhaps, understanding that it is an exchange. We don't accept for a moment that the submission of the voluminous materials by Mr. Lukic following his examination is the equivalent of our submission of the linked documents and the very narrow submission of the linked documents, akin to precisely was done with expert Subotic as we mentioned repeatedly. So that was, as you recall, from the manner or presentation and the manner of submission when expert Subotic was here, Mr. Weber noted that he could expedite matters simply by providing the Court with a very limited number of investigative files or similar documents that were linked to the report that -- of incidents that were discussed in the report or specific source materials. And he -- and those matters were, in fact, admitted before the expert had concluded, against the possibility that Mr. Weber might have to actually go through a more formal process with the witness on the stand for that. Now, and we, throughout the discussion about the Poparic materials, we followed that precise format; a very limited number of documents specifically arising from the expert's report that could have been presented but were more efficiently dealt with in this manner. Now, that would contrast to that in a very dramatic way to Mr. Lukic' list which is a dramatic list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Drama is expressed in numbers what, how many ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Lukic could tell us [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It changes all the time, but it is cut down from 28 pages to 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's just the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can see the Table 1 or two documents on a page but I don't -- I haven't counted yet I can count if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there's no need to do that immediately and I have an impression of what it approximately is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's around 46, I was just told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Forty-five or 46. This large.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And it's not just the number of documents, not just the quantity, but it's the nature of the documents, the quality of materials being submitted, after testimony, without hearing what the witness might have to say about it, without having cross-examined on it, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if we want to have this really formal, then we proposed all the documents from our updated list to be admitted and, of course, the Prosecution can then object if they want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a closer look at it anyhow. Of course, if there are any specific objections already against some of the documents we'd like to know. One of the problems the Chamber may face, Mr. Lukic, is that if you -- in order to illustrate a certain portion of the report, if you tender then a longer document, is it then your intention that we look only at that portion of the document which illustrates the testimony or the portion of the report of the witness, or because if everything is in evidence, this Chamber has a habit of considering everything, what is in that document. So, therefore, that may ... otherwise, of course, you would be invited to limit it to that portion of a document and, again, I have not looked at the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We could limit ourselves to only portions of the document and you have footnote when that is already mentioned so if you just for you to be able to check in the document, otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the issue, whether we are presented with new evidence or whether we are presented with an opportunity to verify the accuracy of what the witness has quoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can assure that it is just for you to verify if the quotation in this work is accurate or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's hereby on the record. The change will consider whether or not we can work on that basis, because that leaves open discussions later on what is still verification, whether it can look one paragraph before, after, same page, next page. We'll consider that, but it's clear you want to give us an opportunity to verify the accuracy of the sources this expert witness has relied on. We'll consider the matter and we'll then deal with both your lists. If there's any comment from you on the Prosecution's list or the other way around, then we'd like to hear from you as soon as possible. Any other matter? In relation to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No -- no distinction additional matter. No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I owe, Your Honours, one explanation. During the testimony of Mr. Bruce Bursik, we challenged past of Mr. Nikolic, and I wrongly told you that he was charged according to the paragraph 167 and I told you, I was on my feet, that it is counterfeiting money, which is not true. It is next paragraph, 168, I missed by one and 167 is trading in gold coins, foreign currency and other foreign bills. So, and the Prosecution uploaded it under number 65 ter 33236 and the translation into English is not complete yet. We are awaiting for that, and I promised Ms. Hasan that I will do this so she can confirm if I did this correctly or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: She's smiling, so she has certainly confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Yes, that's correct, the English language translation has been uploaded, and Your Honours, you'll find the question that had been asked specifically about Article 167 at transcript page 38885 and what we've uploaded as Mr. Lukic has said is the original Article 167 from 1976 and there were two subsequent amendments, one in 1984 and one in 1987, which can also be found in that -- that upload that we've made available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that the parties now agree on what Article 168 says? And do we need it in evidence at all or could you stipulate that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can stipulate that I was wrong and that's what -- what is said in the document. We have no problem for having it uploaded, but we can stipulate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, any need to still add more to the evidence although?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, if that is satisfactory to the Bench as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless you expect us to go into the whole of the case law on selling gold, but I don't think that you would. I think the uploading was mainly to settle the slight dispute and the dispute has been settled by now. Then I think we leave it to that for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can you just repeat the 65 ter number that you referred to at page 77, line 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I -- Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. One more matter that arises from the testimony of Mr. Bursik and Your Honours raised this on the 22nd of October at transcript page 40253 to 40257, and it relates to three excerpts from documents that the Defence used during the direct examination. These were provisionally admitted, subject to our submissions on their admissibility and we will not be objecting to the three excerpts tendered by the Defence, and they are D1322, MFI; D1323, MFI; and D1324, MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, D1322, D1323, and D1324 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just one final matter. And that's a correction that needs to be made to the Srebrenica trial video; that's P01147, as well as its accompanying stills book P01148. It relates to DutchBat soldier footage of a convoy of buses leaving Potocari to Kladanj. In our video and in our stills book, it is recorded that this footage was taken on the 13th of July, 1995. That is an error, and that footage was taken on the 12th of July, 1995. We have uploaded, under 65 ter number 28781A, a correction to the trial record which sets out specifically where in the trial video a correction needs to be made and in the stills book. And, of course, there is a transcript that accompanies the video and that too, on pages 78 in the English and 73 in the B/C/S, should reflect the correct date, 12th July 1995. So we propose, and we've discussed the matter with the Defence and we have their agreement on this, that this correction that we've uploaded be admitted so that the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a look at it because it's a bit uncommon to make a correction to a video. But we'll have a look at it and then we'll -- we -- it's on the record that the parties do not disagree on the matter. Therefore, a decision in due course will follow. We also have to find out whether, for example, this is the best technical way. Because the stills book can be amended. So, therefore, then you would have the complete one. But we'll consider what's the best technical way of doing it. I mean, to change a video is a bit difficult. Therefore, the submission perhaps adds --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, you're right it would be difficult for us to change the video. In fact creating a new ERN number, a new compilation. Same goes for the stills book. The reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Stills book is easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Certainly. We just have to track down where witnesses have been referred to certain pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a look at it and it's clear that the parties do not disagree. Any other matter? If not, I have a few of such exciting matters again as I often address. The first one is -- deals with the ICTY witness statement given by Tarik Zunic on the 10th of November, 1995 which on the 29th of October of this year was admitted into evidence as D1337. The Chamber notes, however that it was already admitted into evidence as part of Exhibit P1945, and that is the Rule 92 bis package of witness Tarik Zunic. And the Chamber therefore instructs the Registry to vacate Exhibit D1337. Next one is about D1334. On the 28th of October, 2015, this exhibit, a video, was admitted into evidence the Chamber puts on the records that contrary to what was previously stated on the record it is not a four-second video but an eight-minute video that was admitted into evidence. The Chamber also notes that this eight-minute video contains dialogue and that a transcript of the dialogue is not available on e-court. And the Chamber would like to know whether the Defence wants to rely on the dialogue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will have to go back to the video, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll -- we'll hear from you later. Another opportunity perhaps would be to limit the excerpt but we'll hear from you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we hear not later than next week, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm just trying to check if it's on our list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you wouldn't mind, I'd prefer to already continue. We hear from you not later than next week. Then, I have item, a remaining issue from the testimony of Sveto Veselinovic. On the 12th of November of last year during the testimony of Sveto Veselinovic, Exhibit D778, a video, was admitted into evidence. And I refer to transcript page 28247. The Chamber notes that the portion of the video from 3 minutes, 57 seconds through 6 minutes, 12 seconds, has dialogue but an English transcript has not been uploaded into e-court. The Chamber contacted the Defence on the 30th of July and on the 13th of October 2015, via e-mail, asking if it intended to rely on that part of the video and, if so, notifying it that an English transcript would be needed. Given that the Chamber has not heard from the Defence on the matter, the Chamber understands that the Defence does not intend to rely on the dialogue in that part of the video. Then, I move to my last item, related to D1227. On the 8th of September, 2015 during the testimony of Radoje Vojvodic, an ICRC report was marked for identification. The Chamber has reviewed the documents and finds that even though there were no questions asked of the witness in relation to the content of the document, its content is related to the subject matter of the witness's testimony. D1227 is admitted, under seal. No matters remaining. We'll adjourn for the day, and we'll resume, Monday, the 9th of November, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 9th day of November, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.
